candidate_relations.reason: The reference diagnosis requires identification of two distinct Plasmodium species (P. falciparum evidenced by appliqué/accolé ring forms, multiply-infected RBCs, high parasitemia, and positive HRP2 on RDT; P. ovale evidenced by ovalocytes with enlarged chromatin dots and fimbriated RBCs) as a co-infection. 'Malaria, acute' is the correct parent category but lacks both the species-level and co-infection specificity that are the defining components of the benchmark diagnosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Names the parent disease category (acute malaria) but omits the required dual-species specificity: Plasmodium falciparum AND Plasmodium ovale co-infection

case_quality_flags: Strong morphologic and RDT evidence supports P. falciparum (HRP2-positive, appliqué forms, multiply-infected RBCs, 3.5% parasitemia) plus P. ovale (ovalocytes, larger chromatin dots); PCR confirmation pending but morphology is diagnostic
Epidemiologic exposure window (19 years since West Africa visit) makes P. ovale hypnozoite reactivation plausible given its long latency
